column1: # #409 — the catalogue of candidate arms, one row each. Tab separated.
# Columns: arm, the EMA momentum at step 0, the momentum at the end of the EMA
# ramp, the EMA ramp length, the DECAY ramp length, the backbone seed. A `-` in
# a column is a flag the arm does NOT pass.
# Add a row here and nothing else changes: every script, guard and figure reads
# this file.
# THIS FILE IS A CATALOGUE, NOT A QUEUE. The search picks its arms one round at
# a time, and each round reads the scores of the round before it. So some rows
# never ran. `notes/search_protocol.md` holds the rule. The section "What the
# run actually spent" gives what each row reached. Read that section before you
# quote a row.
# Every arm runs #373's cell `arm6_v2_combab_alignT` at k = 32 under the `mean`
# reduction, with `--align-target teacher`. `study.sh` holds those values. Only
# the three momentum columns, the decay ramp and the seed change between two
# rows.
# One extra factor in front of L_rep. It starts at 1.0 and falls linearly to
# 0.0 at the RAMP. The two ends are the card's, and they are in `study.sh`.
# THE RAMP IS COLUMN 5 HERE. Four rows hold one schedule and one seed and
# differ in the ramp alone, so a table without that column cannot tell them
# apart. Fifteen rows take the card's own 10,000 steps. `dec_ramp5k_m080`,
# `dec_ramp20k_m080` and `dec_ramp30k_m080` carry 5,000, 20,000 and 30,000.
# `results/scores.csv` records the ramp of every scored arm.
# The card's "The arms" section says the sweep's table is a guide and not a
# list, and that another schedule is allowed with a reason. So the first
# backbones go to SCHEDULES.
# The align target is the EMA teacher. Past the ramp the decay has taken L_rep
# out, so L_align is the whole main loss and the teacher is the only target
# left. The schedule sets how fast that teacher moves. That is what makes it
# the first axis worth the backbones.
# The DECAY RAMP is the second axis. The rounds opened it when every tested
# momentum had lost to the card's target.
# The number that ranks an arm is the momentum it HOLDS at the 40,000-step
# stop, not the momentum its command line names: `dec_m090_r60` and
# `dec_m090_r200` both name 0.9 and hold 0.967 and 0.920.
# The score beside each row is the SAME schedule with NO decay, from
# reports/2026-08-19_ema_momentum_k32/ema_momentum_k32.md. It is what the arm
# is read against. A schedule with no score there is one the sweep never ran.
#   dec_s20        0.940 at the stop. 1.1507, the second best of the sweep.
#   dec_s22        0.940. Same schedule, second seed.
#   dec_s23        0.940. Same schedule, third seed.
#   dec_s24        0.940. Same schedule, fourth seed. 1.1491 with no decay,
#                  which is the number the card asks an arm to beat.
#   dec_s25        0.940. Same schedule, fifth seed.
#                  These five started before the axis changed to the schedule.
#                  Three of them reached 40,000 steps and hold this card's own
#                  seed spread, which is what separates a small gain.
#   dec_m090_fix   0.900. 1.1819. The teacher never slows. It is the only arm
#                  whose momentum is the same at step 10,000 and at the stop,
#                  so it separates "a slow teacher" from "a teacher that slows
#                  while the decay runs".
#   dec_m090_r60   0.967. 1.1873. Same start as `dec_s20`, faster ramp.
#   dec_m095_fix   0.950. 1.1907. It holds 0.950 with NO ramp, between the
#                  0.940 and the 0.967 of the two ramp arms. So the three tell
#                  the reached value from the shape that reaches it.
#   dec_m099_fix   0.990. The sweep never ran it, and it is the one arm past
#                  the sweep's range. L_rep carries the negatives, and the
#                  decay removes them at step 10,000. A slow teacher is the
#                  standard guard against collapse when negatives are absent,
#                  so the decay should move the best momentum UP. This arm is
#                  where that move would show. 0.99 is also train.py's own
#                  default momentum.
#   dec_m090_r200  0.920. 1.1784. Same start as `dec_s20`, slower ramp. With
#                  `dec_m090_fix` and `dec_m090_r60` it gives one ordered row
#   dec_m080_r200  0.840. 1.1782, the sweep's second best and its only good arm
#                  away from 0.9. It is the fast-teacher end. Under the decay a
#                  fast teacher has no repel term beside it, so this arm says
#                  whether the fast end survives. A collapse here is a result.
#   dec_m095_r100  0.970. 1.2130. It reaches almost what `dec_m090_r60` reaches,
#                  0.970 against 0.967, from a different start. The sweep
#                  separated that pair by 0.0257, so the pair says whether the
#                  start or the reached value sets the score.
#   dec_m070_fix   0.700. The sweep never ran it. ADDED MID-RUN. `dec_m080_r200`
#                  at 0.840 scored the best of the decay arms, so the run
#                  carried the ladder past the sweep's fast end to find the
#                  turn.
#   dec_m050_fix   0.500. The sweep never ran it. ADDED MID-RUN, for the same
#                  reason, one step further out.
#   dec_ramp30k_m080, dec_ramp20k_m080, dec_ramp5k_m080
#                  0.840, the schedule and the seed of `dec_m080_r200`. ADDED
#                  MID-RUN, when every tested momentum had lost to the card's
#                  target. They move the DECAY RAMP and not the schedule, to
#                  10,000 the four give one ordered row on the ramp axis.
#                  0.840, the schedule, the ramp and the cell of
#                  `dec_m080_r200`, at seed 20260524. It is a REPEAT SEED, and
#                  it gives the error bar of the best score of this card.
# Seed 20260521 stays OUT. It lost the contrastive task once in the sweep, so a
# collapse there could not be read as the decay's.
# The score is the 97-config GIFT-Eval GM-Relative MASE, in
# `results/scores.csv`. The AUC verdict is in `results/auc_verdicts.tsv`.
#   arm                reached  score     what happened
#   dec_s20             40,000  1.2670    held the contrastive task
#   dec_m099_fix        40,000  1.2849    held. Resumed as `_r2` after a crash
#   dec_m080_r200       40,000  1.2352    held. The best score of the card
#   dec_ramp5k_m080     40,000  1.2727    held
#   dec_m050_fix        10,600  none      LOST the contrastive task at 10,162
#   dec_m080_r200_s24  running  none      started 08-26 23:57, gpu 0. The
#                                         repeat seed of the best arm
#   dec_s23             22,900  none      an outside SIGKILL at 14:18 on 08-23
#   dec_s25             22,700  none      the same kill, the same second
#                                        Both are seed repeats of a schedule
#                                        already measured at three seeds, so
#                                        neither started again. Their rows stay
#                                        here because the card asks for the
#                                        contrastive AUC of EVERY run.
#   dec_m090_r60           100  none      the Hub outage of 08-23 18:48
#   dec_m095_fix             0  none      the same outage
#   dec_m090_fix        never started
#   dec_m090_r200       never started
#   dec_m095_r100       never started
# `dec_s26` also never started, so it has no row: it wrote a header and no step.
# WHY THE SEARCH LEFT THE EMA AXIS. Five schedules hold 0.500, 0.700, 0.840,
# 0.940 and 0.990 at the stop, and every one of them loses to the card's target
# of 1.1491 by 0.0861 or more. That is nearly four times this card's measured
# seed spread of 0.022. A sixth schedule on the same axis cannot close that
# gap, so the round after it moved the decay ramp instead.
# `launch.sh` deals the rows round-robin over the two cards, so each card holds
# a spread of the momentum ladder and one lost card takes no whole end of it.
# A row that moves the seed carries it in its name, so a reader never takes two
# seeds of one arm for two treatments.
# L_rep carries the negatives of this objective. Past step 10,000 nothing
# pushes the representations apart. The trainer writes the contrastive AUC to
# the `auc` column of <run>_losses.csv every step, and #409 adds `rep_w`,
# `l_rep` and `l_align` beside it. Read the AUC of every arm and name the step
# any run leaves the 0.95 to 0.98 band the sweep's healthy arms held.
